title: Counting $\ell$-interval Fubini rankings through their parking outcome
summary: Fubini rankings with $n$ competitors are $n$-tuples with entries in $[n]=\{1,2,3,\ldots, n\}$ that encode the conclusion of a race that allows ties. Since Fubini rankings are parking functions, we can study their parking outcomes, which are permutations encoding the final parking order of the cars using the Fubini ranking as a preference list. We establish that the number of Fubini rankings with $n$ competitors having a fixed parking outcome $π$ is given by $2^{n-k}$, where $k$ denotes the number of runs in $π$.
